ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a horizontal straight line intersects an oblique line. At this intersection point, the angle on the upper right side of the horizontal line is labeled 40°, and the angle on the lower right side of the horizontal line is labeled ∠7. The figure also shows a right-angle mark for AB and BC at point B, but this condition does not need to be used directly for finding ∠7 at this intersection point. Reasoning: ∠7 and the angle labeled 40° are adjacent at the same intersection point, and their non-common sides are on the same oblique line in opposite directions, so they form a linear pair. The two angles of a linear pair are supplementary, so ∠7 = 180° - 40° = 140°.

method.method_draft: From the image, locate the crossing where the slanted ray meets the horizontal line: the angle above the line on the right is labeled 40°, and ∠7 is the adjacent angle below the line on the right at the same intersection. From the text, the target is ∠7; the condition \(\overline{AB} \perp \overline{BC}\) is not needed for this local angle. Since adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary, \(\angle 7 = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ\).
